samples.summary: New Apply guard is unreachable when edit mode was entered with no link at the caret, so the "silently rewrite a link the user never opened" case it exists to prevent stays reachable
samples.evidence: `handleApply` gates on `editingHref !== null && editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref` (docs-link-popover.tsx:169), and `editingHref` is set to `editRequest.initialUrl || null` (line 100), where `initialUrl` is `editor.getLinkAtCursor() ?? ""` (docs-view.tsx:466). Sequence: press ⌘K with a selection over plain text (or an empty caret) → `initialUrl === ""` → `editingHref === null` → guard permanently off for that popover instance; then click inside an existing hyperlink (mousedown collapses the selection and places the caret in it) → click Apply. `insertLink` re-reads live state at Apply time, takes the collapsed-caret branch (editor.ts:3639-3646) and calls `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` on whatever link the caret landed in. With Part A of this change the blast radius is larger than before: for a self-labelled link the display *text* is destroyed too (link-run.ts:104-111), not just the href. The guard's own comment claims it prevents exactly this. Not attacker-controlled, so impact is unintended document mutation rather than a privilege bypass.

samples.summary: Apply guard compares href strings rather than link identity, so a second link with the same href passes it and is rewritten instead of the one the popover was opened on
samples.evidence: The guard is `editor.getLinkAtCursor() !== editingHref` (docs-link-popover.tsx:169). `getLinkAtCursor` returns only the href string (editor.ts:3713), so if the document contains two distinct hyperlinks sharing one href (trivially common — the same URL linked twice, or an autolinked URL repeated), opening the popover on link A and then clicking into link B satisfies the equality check. `insertLink` then rewrites B's href and, when B is self-labelled, B's display text (link-run.ts:104-111). The comment at lines 50-55 asserts the href was chosen over a boolean specifically to stop "a silent edit to a link the user never opened"; that property does not hold for duplicate hrefs. A stable link/run identity (block id + run start/end captured at open time) would close it.

samples.summary: normalizeLinkUrl validates with isSafeUrl but never rejects hasUrlAlteringChars, and this change newly copies that same unnormalized string into document text as well as the href
samples.evidence: `normalizeLinkUrl` returns the *raw* trimmed input whenever `isSafeUrl(url)` is true (url-detect.ts:14-18) and does not call `hasUrlAlteringChars`, even though core documents that function as `isSafeUrl`'s precondition for any caller that goes on to emit the validated string (core/src/url/index.ts:37-47, issue #988). `new URL('https://ex.com/a\nb')` deletes the LF and reports protocol `https:`, so a URL carrying a tab/LF/CR or an interior space is accepted verbatim; `rewriteLinkHrefInPlace` now writes that string into inline *text* via `doc.insertText` (link-run.ts:108) in addition to the href, on both the docs and text-box paths. I could not build an exploit chain: `javascript:` cannot survive the WHATWG rewrite (tested `java\nscript:`, leading `\t`/space — all rejected), link opening is gated on `isSafeUrl` with `noopener,noreferrer` (text-editor.ts:1824, 2177), and the markdown/PDF emitters re-gate with `hasUrlAlteringChars` (serialize/markdown.ts:328, export/pdf-painter.ts:903). So this is hardening: an href/text pair whose bytes differ from what the gate judged, plus a control character reaching inline text where the model assumes none. Searched: all call sites of normalizeLinkUrl, isSafeUrl and hasUrlAlteringChars across the repo, plus core/test/url.test.ts.
searchedFor: grep insertLink call sites (frontend + docs + slides)
